cases.purpose: An injected close(2) EIO on one of three devices is reported once with the device name and 'close', sets status 1 without aborting the later device (all five flush ioctls ran), leaves no descriptor referring to the fixture files, and a following clean run succeeds.
cases.oracle: Seccomp-notify supervisor that fails close(2) of exactly the fixture file with EIO after replacing the descriptor by /dev/null (so the fixture file is really released), plus reviewed system-sequence.py for fsync; expected diagnostics follow the builtin's documented error format (<device>: close: <errno>) and the /proc/PID/fd listing is the descriptor oracle.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.

files.inner.sh:
me=$BASHPID
n_ref() { local c=0 f t; for f in /proc/$me/fd/*; do t=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$f" 2>/dev/null); [[ $t == */$1* ]] && c=$((c+1)); done; echo $c; }
last() { mapfile -t L < err.txt; REPLY=${L[-1]}; REPLY=${REPLY#*$1: }; }
blockdev --flushbufs img1 img2 img3 2>err.txt; rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' $rc
mapfile -t L < err.txt; echo "diagnostics=${#L[@]}"; for l in "${L[@]}"; do echo "  ${l#*blockdev: }"; done
echo "fds-referring-to-img=$(n_ref img)"
blockdev --flushbufs img1 img3 2>err.txt; echo "clean-run status=$?"

cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
: > img1; : > img2; : > img3
/usr/bin/python3 closeinj.py img2 inj.log --ioctl 0x1261 -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc inner.sh
echo "driver=$?"
echo "log: $(/usr/bin/grep -c 'ioctl 0x1261' inj.log) flush ioctls, $(/usr/bin/grep -c '^close img2 -> EIO' inj.log) injected close"
cases.stdout:
status=1
diagnostics=1
  img2: close: Input/output error
fds-referring-to-img=0
clean-run status=0
driver=0
log: 5 flush ioctls, 1 injected close

cases.purpose: An injected fsync EIO makes mkfs report 'fsync: Input/output error' with status 1 and close its image descriptor (none refers to the image afterwards); mkfs of the same image without injection succeeds.
cases.oracle: Seccomp-notify supervisor that fails close(2) of exactly the fixture file with EIO after replacing the descriptor by /dev/null (so the fixture file is really released), plus reviewed system-sequence.py for fsync; expected diagnostics follow the builtin's documented error format (<device>: close: <errno>) and the /proc/PID/fd listing is the descriptor oracle.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.
cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-sequence.py
/usr/bin/truncate -s 1M m.img
/usr/bin/python3 $H --errno fsync:EIO -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc inner.sh
echo "driver=$?"
mkfs m.img 2>/dev/null; echo "after-injection-run status=$?"
cases.stdout:
status=1 last-diagnostic=[fsync: Input/output error]
fds-referring-to-image=0
driver=0
after-injection-run status=0
